component.name: OpennComm
component.summary: Speak using head movement, blinks or morse code

description.p: OpennComm is assistive communication for people who cannot speak or use their hands. A webcam tracks head movement and blinks; those become letters, words and spoken sentences.
Everything runs on your own machine. Speech recognition, sentence suggestion and the synthesised voice are all local, so nothing a patient says is sent anywhere.

Everything it needs is in the package: the face-tracking, speech-recognition and answer-writing models, and two neural voices, one woman's and one man's. There is nothing to download afterwards and no account to create, which is why it is a large download. It works on a machine that has never been connected to a network.
OpennComm is not a medical device and must not be relied on for clinical decisions or emergency communication. See the DISCLAIMER shipped with this package.

The packages now carry every model and both voices. Installing one gives a working system with nothing left to download: previously the speech recognition, the written answers and the neural voice all needed a further 1.2 GB fetched by hand, and nothing on screen said so.
First packaged release. Head movement, blinks and morse spelling all work; speech recognition, answer suggestion and the synthesised voice all run locally. Ships as a .deb and an .rpm.
